cells.quote: The mean dry assessment scores below demonstrate improvements for all participants from attempt 1 to 2 (Fig. 3 and Table 2). Participants’ dry M-GEARS scores (n = 47) for all four tasks demonstrated a mean difference of 18.72 (SD 20.38, 95% CI 12.74–24.71, p < 0.001)
cells.note: All participants were considered novice robotic surgeons; assessments occurred at the beginning and end of a four-day pre-clinical curriculum.

O.outcome_detail: OCHRA error scores in dry tasks

cells.quote: Dry tasks’ OCHRA assessments demonstrated a significant reduction in participants’ (n = 35) errors with a mean difference of –30.57 (SD 31.36, 95% CI – 41.34 to – 19.80, p < 0.001).
cells.note: The negative mean difference indicates fewer errors at the end of training.

O.outcome_detail: summative dry-task and cyst-model M-GEARS scores

result.effect: pass mean 86.05% versus fail mean 70%; mean difference 16.05 percentage points, SE 2.06, 95% CI 11.90–20.22, p < 0.001

cells.quote: Mean total M-GEARS scores for the summative dry tasks second attempt and the cyst model were compared between pass and fail groups. The means were 86.05% and 70% for pass and fail participants respectively (mean difference 16.05, SE 2.06, 95% CI 11.90–20.22, p < 0.001).
cells.note: Thirty of the total 47 participants (63.82%) achieved the pass mark of 80% or over; pass/fail status was determined by the curriculum assessment.

O.outcome_detail: Learning-process survey ratings were higher for the m-learning group on teacher competence, lesson interest, perceived learning, group size, and teacher-student interaction.

cells.quote: There were higher ratings in the responses from the m-learning group compared with the control group for the items the teacher was competent (p < .001), lessons were interesting (p = .016), I was able to learn a lot (p = .022), the size of the groups was optimal (p = .002) and the teacher-student interaction was adequate (p = .008).
cells.note: Post-program participant survey; the study reports p values but no printed effect size.

O.outcome_detail: Learning-process survey ratings for combining theory and practice and preference for another learning group.

cells.quote: There were no significant differences between groups for the items theory and practice were well combined (p = .114) and I would like to have been in another learning group (p = .185).
cells.note: Non-significant differences are coded ns because no equivalence test or adequate-power justification for these outcomes is reported.
